status: Research attempt; no new theorem or review movement
target: Remove the unbounded natural alternating/symmetric primitive cost from the existing hereditary wreath criterion.
attempt: Use a primitive element and a monic degree-n polynomial to replace a rank-n multiplication table by n coefficients, allowing degree polynomial in n and hoping for n^(O(n)) connected components.
exact_budget_check: On P1 with infinity as divisor and a hypothetical algebra generator of pole order at most one, the ith characteristic coefficient is a section of O(i). Independent coefficient coordinates have dimension sum_{i=1}^n(i+1)=n(n+3)/2. Thus this particular unrestricted coefficient atlas is already quadratic before isomorphism witnesses. This is not a lower bound for every possible presentation of the actual geometric sublocus.
local_vs_global_distinction: The proved sparse DVR atlas has O(n) coordinates over a fixed residue field and fixed residue polynomial when normalized different is bounded. It supplies neither a uniform global pole presentation for that residue polynomial nor controlled coefficient functions on exceptional curves. Its own unresolved-global-input remark explicitly leaves this problem open.
why_existing_inputs_do_not_close_it: The previously proved superperfect-product example already has all-characteristic quadratic representation growth and linear low-degree cohomology bounds but is not finitely generated. Therefore a new purely abstract implication from those estimates would be false. Its disjoint odd-cycle argument also gives linear minimal representation dimension for large alternating groups, so merely changing the faithful defining-characteristic matrix model cannot remove the natural-action quadratic loss.
remaining_required_input: A genuine global exceptional-neighbourhood algebra presentation with O(n) total geometric parameters and polynomial-degree equations, exact coverage of all finite etale algebras, and an all-coefficient-ring isomorphism comparison. No such construction has been obtained.
source_scope: Fresh full internal proofs above, with their previously recorded primary source dependencies; no new primary proof is claimed read.
